test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-3) Official Paper (Held On: 17 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Second Five-Year Plan was aimed at laying emphasis on ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**industrial sector**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan**

 
 
• The **second five-year plan gave industries**, mainly heavy industries a lot of attention.
 
• In contrast to the First Five Year Plan, which focused mostly on agriculture, the Second Plan encouraged **domestic industrial product production, especially in the growth of the public sector**.
 
• The strategy was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, an economic growth framework created in **1953** by** Indian statistician Prasanta Chandra Mahalanobis**.
 
• The strategy sought to identify the best distribution of investments among productive industries in order to **maximise long-term economic growth**.
 
• It made use of **cutting-edge operations research and optimization approaches** as well as creative uses of **statistical models created by the Indian Statistical Institute**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under the Second Five-Year Plan, the state focused on **consumer goods**, while the first plan's factories helped **boost overall industrial output**.
 
• With assistance from the Soviet Union, Britain (U.K.), and West Germany, hydroelectric power projects and five steel plants were built in **Bhilai, Durgapur, and Rourkela, respectively**.
 
• Production of **coal** increased.
 
• In the northeast, more **railway lines were constructed**.
 
• In total, **48 billion rupees** were allotted for the Second Five-Year Plan in India.
 
• The following sectors received this sum: c**ommunications and transportation, miscellaneous, social services, power and irrigation, and other**.
 
• **Actual growth was** **4.27 per cent **compared to the **target growth rate of 4.5 per cent**.
